Apple launched the iPhone 17 last September and began counting down to when this new flagship would break a record set 15 years ago. That record would take over a year to break, but according to current rumours, the iPhone 17 will be the first model to take the crown.

The iPhone 4 had an unusually long sales run

The record is held by the iPhone 4, which went on sale in June 2010 and remained Apple's top-tier iPhone until October 2011. Because Apple shifted its flagship launch cycle from summer to autumn that year, the iPhone 4 held its position for nearly 16 months.

For consumers planning to 'wait for the iPhone 5', this was an especially frustrating period. Instead, Apple released the iPhone 4S, which looked nearly identical to the iPhone 4. The changes were hidden inside the body: Siri made its debut, camera performance improved, and processing power also got a boost.

Technically, the iPhone 4 also had several launch moments. US carrier AT&T, Apple's exclusive US partner, released the phone first. Six months later, Verizon became the second US carrier partner. After a ten-month delay, the much-anticipated white version finally arrived.

Since then, no iPhone has managed to replicate the iPhone 4's 15-month flagship sales run. The closest was the iPhone 11 Pro, which held its position for 13 months while the iPhone 12 was delayed due to the pandemic. Other exceptions exist, such as the gaps between the iPhone SE, SE 2, and iPhone 16e, each exceeding four years, but these are deliberate arrangements, not flagship cycles.

iPhone 17 expected to break the record (with a key difference)

The iPhone 18 is not expected to arrive until spring 2027. This means the iPhone 17 will hold the top spot in Apple's mainstream lineup for roughly 18 months, surpassing the iPhone 4's record and setting a new benchmark for the longest sales run of a standard iPhone.

Model Launch Replaced by Duration at top iPhone 17 September 2025 iPhone 18, Spring 2027 (expected) ~550 days, ~18 months (projected) iPhone 4 iPhone 4S 477 days, ~15.7 months iPhone 11 Pro iPhone 12 Pro 399 days, ~13.1 months iPhone (2007) iPhone 3G 378 days, ~12.4 months

A key difference between the iPhone 4 era and today is the emergence of the Pro lineup. The transition from iPhone 4 to iPhone 4S was an upgrade drought for consumers expecting new features.

I think it really depends on how you define 'flagship model'

During this cycle from iPhone 17 to iPhone 18, the Pro models will still update annually and are expected to launch alongside Apple's first foldable iPhone.

The foldable iPhone will be the most dramatic hardware change in iPhone history, but the iPhone 17 is still expected to claim the crown for the longest gap between standard flagship models.

The shortest iPhone cycle

Incidentally, the record for the shortest iPhone upgrade cycle may come as a surprise. The first to come to mind is the cycle from iPhone 12 to iPhone 13, which lasted only 11 months after Apple adjusted its pace following pandemic-related delays.

However, although the iPhone X launched in September 2017, it did not go on sale until November 2017, and the iPhone XS replaced it just 10 months later.
